intro: Lesson 29. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: فَصَبَّ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّكَ سَوْطَ عَذَابٍ (١٣) إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِٱلْمِرْصَادِ (١٤) فَأَمَّا ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ إِذَا مَا ٱبْتَلَىٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَأَكْرَمَهُۥ وَنَعَّمَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّىٓ أَكْرَمَنِ (١٥) وَأَمَّآ إِذَا مَا ٱبْتَلَىٰهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّىٓ أَهَٰنَنِ (١٦) كَلَّا ۖ بَل لَّا تُكْرِمُونَ ٱلْيَتِيمَ (١٧) وَلَا تَحَٰٓضُّونَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلْمِسْكِينِ (١٨)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment.
Indeed, your Lord is in observation.
And as for man, when his Lord tries him and [thus] is generous to him and favors him, he says, "My Lord has honored me."
But when He tries him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me."
No! But you do not honor the orphan
And you do not encourage one another to feed the poor.

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-Fajr 89:13-18 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 89:13-18 together without the mushaf.

options: a hamza is in the next word

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 89:13-18 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Recite Al-Fajr 89:1 to 18 to a partner. Partner ticks each ayah.
questions.a: Eighteen ticks; slips noted for home revision.

questions.q: Name all the madds in 89:15 to 16.
questions.a: Munfasil: رَبِّىٓ أَكْرَمَنِ, وَأَمَّآ إِذَا, رَبِّىٓ أَهَٰنَنِ; natural: مَا, ٱبْتَلَىٰهُ, فَيَقُولُ and others.

options: honouring the orphan and feeding the poor
questions.a: A) honouring the orphan and feeding the poor. 89:17 to 18: you do not honour the orphan, and you do not encourage one another to feed the poor.

questions.q: Al-Fajr 89:17: «كَلَّا بَل ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: When Allah gives a person a lot, he says 'my Lord honoured me'; when less, 'my Lord humiliated me' (89:15 to 16). Is wealth really how Allah shows honour?
questions.a: No: both ease and hardship are tests. Honour is in faith and good deeds, such as honouring the orphan and feeding the poor (89:17 to 18).
